Here people are deprived even of the basic necessities of life and are unacquainted with suitable facilities of housing, education, recreation and health. "Most of the world's people live in poverty beyond the imagination of people in rich western countries." (S. Fischer)

Therefore economists think how, by making the speed of economic development fast, people can be given deliverance from poverty.

Concept of economic development (Concept of Economic Development)

Different economists have defined economic development in different ways. For example, Professor Harold Williamson writes in his book “Economic Development”: “By economic development is meant that process (Process) by means of which the people of a country or area, using existing resources, make a reasonable increase in the per capita quantity of goods and services.”

1. Increase in the production of goods and services.

2. The rate of increase in the production of goods and services should be more than the rate of population growth, so that per capita income can increase.

3. The increase in the production of goods occurs with the help of two factors: people and natural resources.

Chapter 8 — Economic Development and Planning

The biggest problem before modern economists is that such principles and practical methods be discovered with whose help backward countries (Backward Countries) can be put on the path of progress, so that their national income increases and the public becomes prosperous. At this time one-fifth of the world’s population (people) is living its life below the poverty line (Poverty Line) (i.e. on an average income of one dollar daily). 49 countries are not only extremely poor, but a worrying matter is that the gap between poor and rich countries too is going on increasing. Its estimate is made thus: at this time the annual gross product (GDP) of the world is thirty trillion (Trillion) dollars, i.e. three hundred kharab or thirty thousand arab dollars, of which 80 per cent comes into the use of only twenty per cent of the world’s population, which lives in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) area (in it these countries are included: America, Canada, Belgium, France, West Germany, Italy, Netherlands, UK, Norway, Sweden and Japan), and the remaining 80 per cent of the world’s population gets a twenty per cent share of world production. Here people are deprived even of the basic necessities of life and are unacquainted with suitable facilities of housing, education, recreation and health. They face poverty, ignorance, disease and unemployment. They are living their lives in such helplessness and poverty which the people of the rich Western countries cannot even imagine:

"Most of the world's people live in poverty beyond the imagination of people in rich western countries." (S. Fischer)

Therefore economists think how, by making the speed of economic development fast, people can be given deliverance from poverty.

Concept of economic development (Concept of Economic Development)

Different economists have defined economic development in different ways. For example, Professor Harold Williamson writes in his book “Economic Development”: “By economic development is meant that process (Process) by means of which the people of a country or area, using existing resources, make a reasonable increase in the per capita quantity of goods and services.”

From its definition it appears that by economic development three things are meant:

1. Increase in the production of goods and services.

2. The rate of increase in the production of goods and services should be more than the rate of population growth, so that per capita income can increase.

3. The increase in the production of goods occurs with the help of two factors: people and natural resources.

paras.text: Professor Arthur Lewis (A. Lewis) defines economic development in these words: “By economic development is meant increase in the production of goods and services.”

sections.theory:
Definition of economic development (Definition)

Professor Arthur Lewis (A. Lewis) defines economic development in these words: “By economic development is meant increase in the production of goods and services.”

Professors Meier and Baldwin (Meier & Baldwin) have given the comprehensive definition of economic development thus: “By economic development is meant such a process (Process) as a result of which the real national income of a country increases over a long period, and if the rate of economic development is more than the rate of population growth, then real per capita income increases.”

In the above definition of economic development three terms have basic importance, whose explanation is necessary:

1. Process (Process)

Economic development is the name of such a process which appears in the form of different changes, and as a total result of which real income increases.

2. Real national income (Reall National Income)

By it is meant that quantity of goods and services which is produced in a country in a particular period. While measuring it, besides the rise and fall of prices, the wear (Depreciation) of machines, buildings and vehicles too should be taken into account.

3. Long period (Long Period)

By it is meant a period of twenty to twenty-five years, because the measurement of economic development (i.e. increase in national production) should be made decade-wise instead of annually.

• Methods of producing goods become better than before.

• With the help of increase in technical skill (Skill), energy (Energy) and capital, the production of goods and services increases.

• A pleasant revolution takes place in social and administrative organisations.

• An increase occurs in total national production and per capita national production; reform and progress take place in technical and scientific information, skill and ways and methods.

• Because of the increase in national production, an increase occurs in national savings and investment, i.e. capital formation (Capital Formation).

• With capital resources increasing, the availability of capital per head becomes more, and as a result the work ability and productivity (Efficiency) of labourers, farmers, workers, artisans, skilled people and workers increases.

• Financial, banking and insurance institutions in the country increase, and facilities of loans and credit increase.

• Means of communications, transport, carriage and news-giving increase.

• The standard of education, health, recreation, culture and civilisation (Civilization) becomes better.

In short, economic development or economic growth (Growth) has been defined thus:

"Economic growth means an increase in the total output of a nation overtime. Economic growth is usually measured as the annual rate of increase in a nation's real G.D.P." (Samuelson)

Definition of economic development (Definition)

Professor Arthur Lewis (A. Lewis) defines economic development in these words: “By economic development is meant increase in the production of goods and services.”

Professors Meier and Baldwin (Meier & Baldwin) have given the comprehensive definition of economic development thus: “By economic development is meant such a process (Process) as a result of which the real national income of a country increases over a long period, and if the rate of economic development is more than the rate of population growth, then real per capita income increases.”

In the above definition of economic development three terms have basic importance, whose explanation is necessary:

1. Process (Process)

Economic development is the name of such a process which appears in the form of different changes, and as a total result of which real income increases.

2. Real national income (Reall National Income)

By it is meant that quantity of goods and services which is produced in a country in a particular period. While measuring it, besides the rise and fall of prices, the wear (Depreciation) of machines, buildings and vehicles too should be taken into account.

3. Long period (Long Period)

By it is meant a period of twenty to twenty-five years, because the measurement of economic development (i.e. increase in national production) should be made decade-wise instead of annually.

• Methods of producing goods become better than before.

• With the help of increase in technical skill (Skill), energy (Energy) and capital, the production of goods and services increases.

• A pleasant revolution takes place in social and administrative organisations.

• An increase occurs in total national production and per capita national production; reform and progress take place in technical and scientific information, skill and ways and methods.

• Because of the increase in national production, an increase occurs in national savings and investment, i.e. capital formation (Capital Formation).

• With capital resources increasing, the availability of capital per head becomes more, and as a result the work ability and productivity (Efficiency) of labourers, farmers, workers, artisans, skilled people and workers increases.

• Financial, banking and insurance institutions in the country increase, and facilities of loans and credit increase.

• Means of communications, transport, carriage and news-giving increase.

• The standard of education, health, recreation, culture and civilisation (Civilization) becomes better.

In short, economic development or economic growth (Growth) has been defined thus:

"Economic growth means an increase in the total output of a nation overtime. Economic growth is usually measured as the annual rate of increase in a nation's real G.D.P." (Samuelson)
